title: HDRTransDC High Dynamic Range Image Reconstruction with Transformer Deformation Convolution

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text cites [Debevec and Malik, 2008] for standard HDR merging, but the classic Debevec and Malik paper 'Recovering high dynamic range radiance maps from photographs' was published in 1997, not 2008.

The authors describe a spatial attention that senses exposure in different regions and 'spatially adaptively selects useful information', but then state the resulting weight δw is 'shared in spatial dimension and fully connected in channel dimension'. A spatially shared weight is a global/channel-wise modulation and cannot perform region-wise spatial selection, contradicting the stated mechanism.

Eq. (2) defines Q from reference tokens and K,V from non-reference tokens, which is cross-attention, but Eq. (3) calls MSA 'multi-headed self-attention'. Self-attention requires Q, K, and V from the same token set; this misdescribes the operation.
